title: Model snapshot bundler: automated tagging, signed bundles, and staged profile broadcasting
creator: Luca Reynolds
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable CI/CD flow that produces deterministic model snapshot bundles, cryptographically signs artifacts, emits performance profiles, and supports staged profile broadcasting (canary -> ramp -> full) with reversible promotion. This ticket implements the bundler + publisher orchestration and validation steps required for safe, auditable onboard of new model revisions.

Background: Current onboarding is manual: model binaries are uploaded, perf profiles are generated ad-hoc, and release engineers perform one-off promotions. This causes rollout delays and occasional mismatches between profile metadata and binary artifacts. The desired flow: 1) PR triggers build pipeline, 2) produce a timestamped snapshot bundle (model weights, tokenizer, config, deterministic build manifest), 3) cosign-style signature and attestation of provenance, 4) publish to artifact registry with opaque pin + human-readable tag, 5) run automated perf harness to produce performance profile, 6) attach profile to the bundle and publish profile manifest, 7) initiate staged-profile broadcast (canary traffic plus health gating), 8) on successful metrics, auto-promote or allow manual promotion/rollback.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pipeline creates deterministic snapshot bundles with reproducible manifest and SHA256 pins.
- Each bundle is signed with the CI signing key and an embedded attestation referencing the build job and source commit.
- A perf profile artifact is generated automatically (latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, memory footprint, quantization notes) and attached to the bundle manifest.
- The publisher exposes a promote/canary API to broadcast profile to runtime with % traffic routing and automatic health gates.
- Rollback path documented and exercised by e2e test that reverts a canary in <5m.
- Audit log entries for each publish/promote action are stored and queryable from the console audit API.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Bundler job: create build container that runs reproducible build, produces model.tar.gz + manifest.json containing input hashes, build env, dependency list, and deterministic file order.
2) Signing step: integrate with KMS-backed signing service (cosign compatible). Sign manifest.json and attach signature as manifest.sig.
3) Publish: push bundle to internal registry (artifactory/s3) under /snapshots/{model}/{semver}-{timestamp}-{shortsha}. Provide opaque pin (content-addressed) and stable alias tags (e.g., latest-stable, latest-canary).
4) Perf harness: spin up test runtime (cost-limited), run canonical workloads defined by the model's eval set in catalog, gather metrics and store profile.json. Attach profile to the bundle and publish combined profile manifest.
5) Staged broadcast orchestrator: orchestration service that accepts promote requests with % ramps and health gates (error rate, latency regressions, quality regressions measured by A/B evals). Implement automatic rollback if thresholds violated.
6) CLI/console: add publish button in Console -> Models and CLI command 'ri bundle publish --canary 5 --ramp 1h'.

Key trade-offs and decisions made so far:
- Reproducibility vs developer velocity: we require hermetic builds for release bundles. That adds CI runtime and caching complexity but reduces latent production mysteries. Decision: enforce hermetic flag for release pipeline; keep iterative dev builds lighter weight in a separate job.
- Signing model: use KMS-backed ephemeral signing keys rotated monthly and record key id in the attestation. Benefit: reduces key theft blast-radius; cost: requires KMS policy changes and SRE involvement.
- Profile generation cost: running perf harness for every push is expensive. We will run a lightweight smoke profile for PRs and a full profile on gated CI for commits to main.
- Promotion gating: prefer metric-driven auto-promote with manual override. Auto-promote applies only when customers flagged for auto on their account; otherwise an approval action is required.

Progress updates and current blockers:
- 2026-02-20: PoC bundler container completed. Deterministic manifest format v1 accepted by PM. (POC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard/pull/212)
- 2026-02-27: Integrated cosign-compatible signature step with staging KMS. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard/pull/227. Tests flaky in CI due to ephemeral KMS credential refresh.
- 2026-03-03: Perf harness prototype collects P50/P95 and tokens/sec. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/model-profiles/profiles?var-model=example-model.
- 2026-03-07: Orchestrator prototype supports canary rollouts and percentage routing; missing audit log persistence and console integration. Orchestrator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/88.
- 2026-03-09: Security review requested. Blocker: KMS IAM must allow CI signer principal to use signing key but deny key export. SRE ticket opened: ENG-78111 (KMS policy update).

Next steps (this ticket):
- Finish robust KMS credential refresh in CI runner (owner: infra team, coordinated by assignee).
- Implement profile manifest schema v1 and attach it to the published bundle (assignee).
- Add audit log write in orchestrator (ENG-77322 will implement storage and query surfaces).
- Add e2e test that simulates a canary promotion and automatic rollback; wire to CI gating (ENG-77323).

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for manifest generation, signature verification, and publish semantics.
- Integration test in staging that goes end-to-end (bundle->sign->publish->profile->promote->rollback) with synthetic traffic.
- Manual code review + security review before enabling auto-promote.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Opt-in teams and internal models only.
- Stage 2: Open to dedicated customers with audit logs enabled.
- Stage 3: Default onboarding flow for all models with required hermetic builds.
